name: LM3670MF-3.3_NOPB
title: 350 mA synchronous step-down converter, 1 MHz, PWM/PFM, SOT-23-5

source.revision: SNVS250F, November 2004, revised February 2016 (orderable addendum dated 1-Nov-2025)

summary: The LM3670 is a small buck regulator with both power switches on chip: a PFET high side and an NFET synchronous rectifier. It takes 2.5 V to 5.5 V, one Li-Ion cell or three NiMH/NiCd cells, and delivers up to 350 mA. Under moderate and heavy loads it switches at a fixed 1 MHz in voltage-mode PWM; at light load it drops into hysteretic PFM, where the quiescent draw is 15 µA typical, and it can run at 100% duty for low dropout. Fixed outputs of 1.2, 1.5, 1.6, 1.8, 1.875 and 3.3 V are offered, plus an adjustable version for 0.7 V to 2.5 V; the outside parts are one inductor and two ceramic capacitors.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input, 2.5 V to 5.5 V; it takes the input filter capacitor to GND.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable. Above 1.3 V the converter runs; below 0.4 V it shuts down. It must not float.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback input. On fixed versions it connects straight to the output capacitor; on the adjustable version it takes the R1/R2 divider tap, regulated to 0.5 V.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switch node, where the on-chip PFET high side meets the NFET rectifier. It drives the inductor, whose saturation current should be above the 750 mA maximum switch current limit.

circuits.title: Typical application, fixed output (Figure 17)
circuits.description: The fixed-voltage LM3670 as a buck converter from a 2.5 V to 5.5 V supply. EN is wired to VIN, so the converter runs whenever the input is up. SW drives L1 into the output node, where COUT smooths the ripple and FB senses the output directly; the internal divider of the fixed versions sets the voltage. CIN supplies the pulsed input current of the PFET switch.
notes: The inductor value reads 10 µF; it is an inductance, 10 µH.

circuits.title: Typical application, adjustable output (Figure 20)
circuits.description: The adjustable LM3670 with an output set between 0.7 V and 2.5 V by R1 and R2, which hold FB at 0.5 V. C1 across R1 places the 10 kHz feedforward zero needed for stability; C2 across R2 adds the pole used at some output voltages. EN is tied to VIN, CIN decouples the input, and L1 with COUT filters the switch node into the output. Every divider and capacitor value for a chosen output comes from the configuration table.

operation.text: Each cycle starts with the PFET on, ramping inductor current from the input into the output capacitor and load. The PFET then turns off and the NFET turns on, so the inductor pulls current up from ground and its current ramps back down. The output capacitor absorbs the difference between inductor and load current.

From roughly 70 mA up to 350 mA the converter runs at a fixed 1 MHz as a voltage-mode controller. Input voltage feedforward cancels the power stage's gain dependence on VIN, which keeps line and load regulation tight. The NFET acts as a synchronous rectifier, cutting the loss an ordinary diode would add at low output voltages.
In PWM mode an internal comparator ends the switch pulse cycle by cycle when the switch current reaches 620 mA typical, protecting the part and the outside components in overload.

The part changes to PFM once discontinuous inductor current, or a peak PMOS current under IMODE, has lasted at least 32 clock cycles. In PFM it holds the output 0.8% to 1.6% (typ) above the PWM level, giving headroom for a load step. Below the high threshold the PMOS turns on until the output passes the high threshold or the current reaches IPFM; the NMOS then conducts until the inductor current reaches zero. At the high threshold both switches turn off and the part sleeps, drawing under 30 µA, until the output sags to the low threshold. If load rises enough to pull the output under the low2 threshold, near the nominal PWM level, the part returns to fixed-frequency PWM. The high threshold is about 1.016 × VOUT and the low1 threshold about 1.008 × VOUT.

When the input approaches the output, the PMOS stays fully on without switching, so the output is held as low as the input allows. The input needed is set by load current through the PFET and inductor resistances (the dropout equation).
An internal soft start limits inrush current, stepping the allowed current up in stages. Start-up takes about 400 µs typical when COUT is 10 µF and the load draws 350 mA.

EN below 0.4 V shuts down the switches, reference, control and bias circuits; above 1.3 V the part runs. EN should be held low during system power-up and whenever the supply is below 2.5 V, and must never float. Shutdown current is 0.1 µA typical.
Besides soft start and current limit, the part has undervoltage lockout (output disabled below 2.4 V typ on VIN) and thermal overload shutdown.

The inductor must not saturate and must keep the ripple small enough for the wanted output ripple. Size its current rating either for load plus half the ripple, or more conservatively for the 700 mA current limit. 10 µH with at least 800 mA saturation current suits most designs, and winding resistance should stay under about 0.3 Ω for efficiency. An unshielded bobbin part is the low-cost choice; noise-sensitive designs need a toroid or shielded bobbin, and a board footprint that fits both types leaves the choice open.

4.7 µF ceramic is enough for most designs; more improves input filtering. It carries the PFET's pulsed current, and low ESR ceramics filter those spikes best. Its surge rating should cover power-up, where the surge current is about the capacitance in µF times the input rise rate in V/µs.

The output capacitor needs enough capacitance and low enough ESR to hold the output through load steps and keep ripple down. ESR varies with frequency and temperature, so it should be taken at a frequency near the switching frequency.

The loop sets VOUT so that FB sits at 0.5 V. R2, from FB to ground, should be at least 100 kΩ so the divider current stays well under the 15 µA quiescent current, but not so large that it picks up noise; 200 kΩ gives 2.5 µA. Outputs from 0.7 V up need a 10 kHz zero from C1 across R1, and at 0.7 V and 2.5 V a 10 kHz pole is added too (C2).
The part runs from a stable supply between 2.5 V and 5.5 V.

Keep the LM3670, inductor and filter capacitors tight together, all within 5 mm (0.2 in) of the IC, with short wide traces, since those traces carry the switching current. Arrange parts so the two half-cycle current loops circulate in the same direction. Join the IC and capacitor grounds with a component-side copper fill and stitch it to any ground plane with several vias, keeping switching current out of the plane. Route the feedback trace directly, close to the IC and away from the noisy power traces, and keep sensitive circuits such as radio IF stages far from the converter. The SW node, which swings between GND and VIN at 1 MHz, is kept clear of ground copper on both sides; CIN, COUT and the feedback parts return to one top-side ground area far from SW; many vias join top and bottom ground; EN reaches its pin by a bottom-side trace so the top ground stays whole; the feedback parts may go on the bottom side so COUT's ground lands nearer the IC ground; and the VIN, SW and VOUT traces and capacitor pads are made wide.
